name: Tessera Corponation Neural Leash NL-2 'Puppeteer'
description:
A flexible weapon that combines a conductive polymer whip with a neural-disruption pulse generator, allowing the operator to deliver targeted cognitive interference through physical contact at range. The Puppeteer is 1.8 meters of polymer cord that, on contact with bare skin or conductive cyberware surfaces, delivers a precisely calibrated electromagnetic pulse that temporarily overrides voluntary motor control — causing the target's muscles to obey the pulse's frequency rather than the target's own neural commands.

The effect is not paralysis — it is involuntary movement. Targets struck by the Puppeteer do not freeze; they move in ways they did not intend, their limbs responding to electromagnetic commands rather than conscious will. At low settings, this manifests as loss of coordination and involuntary jerking. At high settings, the operator can induce specific gross motor patterns — causing a target to drop a held weapon, take a step in a specific direction, or raise their arms. The control is imprecise and cannot produce fine motor manipulation, but the ability to make an opponent's body betray them is tactically devastating.

Tessera developed the NL-2 under a contract from their corrections division for a restraint tool that could control prisoners without physical contact. The weapon's capability has since expanded far beyond its original scope, and the ethical implications of a weapon that puppets another person's body have generated ongoing controversy that Tessera has largely ignored.
legality: Restricted — neural-override weapon, prohibited in most jurisdictions
specifications:
total_length: 1.8 meters
weight: 450 g
contact_type: Conductive polymer on bare skin or cyberware
effect_range: Contact only — requires physical touch
control_precision: Gross motor only — no fine manipulation
power_source: Handle power cell, 40 activations
effect_duration: 5-15 seconds per contact
tactical_use: The Puppeteer is used to control rather than damage. An operator who lands a contact strike can force the target to drop their weapon, move out of cover, or turn to face away — creating openings that would be impossible to achieve through conventional combat. Against augmented targets, the neural override propagates through cybernetic motor pathways with enhanced effect, making the weapon more powerful against the most dangerous opponents. The limitation is the contact requirement — the polymer cord must touch skin or conductive surface, meaning armored targets who deny skin contact are largely immune.
cultural_context: The Puppeteer has crossed a line that even GLMZ's desensitized population finds disturbing. A weapon that takes away bodily autonomy — that makes your own muscles work against you — evokes a specific horror that transcends physical pain. Confirmed incidents of NL-2 use have generated public outrage disproportionate to the weapon's actual damage potential, because the violation is psychological rather than physical. Anti-corporate activists have made the Puppeteer a symbol of corporate control made literal — a corporation that can puppet your body as easily as it puppets your livelihood.
story_hooks: A Puppeteer operator has discovered that sustained contact with a specific type of neural implant creates a persistent connection — the target continues responding to commands even after the whip is withdrawn. Tessera is very interested in this development.

An NL-2 was used during a public arrest, and bystander footage of the target being puppeted against their will has gone viral. The political fallout is threatening Tessera's operating licenses in three districts.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact handle-mounted control unit connected to a coiled polymer whip that hangs like a serpent. The whip itself is thin and sinuous, with a faint iridescent shimmer suggesting conductive fibers woven through flexible polymer. The handle dominates visually — a chunky, ergonomic grip with recessed control surfaces and faintly glowing status indicators that pulse with activity.
physical_description.dimensions: Handle: 12cm length × 4.5cm width × 3cm depth. Whip: 180cm fully extended, 8mm diameter when coiled.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light in hand — the handle feels balanced and substantial (450g total), but the whip adds almost no resistance when deployed. The control unit sits heavy in the palm while the cord trails weightlessly, creating an asymmetrical kinetic feel that demands respect.
physical_description.primary_material: Conductive polymer whip with woven metallic filament matrix. Handle constructed from reinforced thermoplastic composite with embedded haptic feedback actuators.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray polymer body with brushed nickel control panels. The whip displays a pearlescent sheen under light — faint rainbow refraction across its surface from the conductive weave. Worn examples show polymer degradation at the grip and micro-scarring along the whip from repeated deployment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with silver accent panels. Status LEDs glow cold blue (standby) or electric violet (active discharge). Faint green trace lines mark conductive pathways along handle seams.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured thermoplastic with microscopic grip-enhancing ridges, worn smooth at the edges from use. Cool to the touch. Subtle electrical tingle at fingertips when powered on.
distinctive_features: Three-stage recessed control pad on handle thumb-rest (low/medium/high neural override intensity)
Pulsing violet LED strip along the handle spine that intensifies during discharge
Microscopic conductive filaments visible as a faint metallic weave throughout the whip — appears almost opalescent in certain light
Emergency dump valve at handle base (pressure relief for thermal overload)
Haptic feedback micro-actuators in grip provide tactile confirmation of power cell status
Thin power distribution cable running internally down the whip to the contact point
Coiling mechanism at base allows whip to snap-retract to compact storage mode
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Media Group logos embossed on handle panel (stylized spiral symbol). Serial number laser-etched on base plate. Small warning glyph (crossed-out brain symbol) stamped below control pad. Cryptic regulatory restriction codes printed in micron-sized text along the grip.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field examples show heavy cosmetic wear — scratched control panels, polymer creasing along the coil, micro-burn marks from repeated discharges. The handle grip often shows dark residue (dried target biofluid/conductive salts) that accumulates despite cleaning. Well-maintained units retain factory finish; combat-used examples develop a patina of small scars and heat-stress discoloration.
